Athena's throughput review 20261105-093605-zwwy named the biggest wait in the pipeline and an architectural change that would remove it. Design that change.

Bottleneck: The landing and rebuild stage: the time from the verifier's end to the landing record has a median of 591.8 of the 616.3 minutes per landed job. All five other stages together take about 22.5 minutes. This stage was 440.1 minutes at the pre...
Stage: landing and rebuild
Proposed change: Build the continuous-landing design (design/continuous-landing.md, D155) and make landing a step the drain drives, not something the job's own worker does. When the verifier passes, the job joins the one ordered landing queue and its worker...
Predicted saving: 570.0 minutes per landed job; the median was 616.3 minutes per landed job when the review ran.
Why: Measured in THROUGHPUT.md: the median per landed job over the last 20 is 616.3 minutes. Of that, landing and rebuild is 591.8; reading 0.6, planning 4.3, producer 13.9, checks 0.6 and verifier 3.1 add up to about 22.5. So nearly all the tim...

A change that implements this design must cite throughput review 20261105-093605-zwwy in its request text. The next throughput review then sets the minutes it measured after that change landed against this prediction.

Acceptance:
- A design note under docs/design/ describes the change and how it removes the bottleneck
- The note states the minutes per landed job the change should save and how the next throughput review measures them
